decision: Use managed browser infrastructure behind a provider-neutral shadow adapter; do not choose a production provider from documentation or sunk cost.
futureCostEvidence: A new Jovie browser host or provider-specific controller would duplicate managed session, action, activity and recovery machinery while adding API churn, site-drift and on-call burden. OpenAI bills model plus hosted-container usage and Cloudflare bills browser duration/concurrency, so supplier economics remain workload evidence rather than an assumed OpenAI win.
switchingCost: Medium: map session events into existing receipts, implement explicit auth/approval UI, review data controls, and replay identical cohorts. No database migration or replacement of deterministic Playwright is required.
rollback: Disable the shadow adapter and keep current Playwright, Cloudflare screenshot capture and product-specific flows unchanged.

reason: Hosting is commodity; select a managed supplier only after same-cohort shadow evidence.
OpenAI supplies the loop, but Jovie workload quality and failure behavior are unproven.
Do not build another host, scheduler or product model around one supplier.
Use provider sign-in requests or approved local profiles; never normalize runtimes by exporting raw cookies.
Origin approval is not confirmation for purchases, writes or destructive actions.
Hosted screenshots are optional output and sensitive; Jovie still owns authorized artifacts and visual oracles.
A completed activity or model answer does not certify the persisted product outcome.
Reuse provider session recovery while retaining Jovie retry budgets, duplicate fencing and uncertain-outcome handling.
Jovie receipts bind the task, tenant, build, activity and independent oracle.
Allowlisted origins/actions, untrusted-page handling and consequential-action consent stay outside provider claims.
One fact/action/receipt seam permits OpenAI, Cloudflare and the current executor to share cohorts.
Provider sessions cannot grant Jovie user, tenant, entitlement or release authority.
Provisioning, analytics normalization, legal/terms gates and native-device behavior remain Jovie product logic.
